title: Environmental Engineering
description: Environmental Engineering covers water and wastewater treatment, air pollution control, solid and hazardous waste, regulations, risk assessment, sustainability, climate impacts, and equitable resilient community systems.

topics.title: Water Quality
topics.description: This section teaches students to define what makes water usable, safe, impaired, or treatable. The aim is to connect field data, environmental chemistry, ecology, and public-health standards.

children.title: Water-quality parameters
children.description: Students learn the core measurements used to describe water condition.

children.title: Dissolved oxygen, BOD, COD, and TOC
Turbidity, color, taste, odor, and temperature
Contaminants and sources
children.description: Students connect pollutants to land use, infrastructure, and natural processes.

children.title: Nutrients, pathogens, metals, and organic chemicals
Stormwater, agriculture, industry, and septic systems
Sampling and monitoring
children.description: Students learn how data quality shapes engineering decisions.

children.title: QA/QC, detection limits, and chain of custody
Field probes, lab methods, and remote sensing
Standards and interpretation
children.description: Students translate measurements into action.

topics.title: Water Treatment Processes
topics.description: This section covers the unit processes that turn raw water into finished water. Students learn process selection, design logic, and performance evaluation.

children.title: Source-water assessment
children.description: Students learn how raw-water quality drives treatment strategy.

children.title: Physical and chemical treatment
children.description: Students study the standard treatment train.

children.title: Disinfection and oxidation
children.description: Students learn how pathogens and chemical contaminants are controlled.

children.title: Process design and operation
children.description: Students evaluate whether treatment meets performance goals.

children.title: Chemical dose, hydraulics, and detention time

topics.title: Wastewater Treatment
topics.description: This section follows wastewater from collection through treatment and residuals management. The point is to see wastewater as both a pollutant load and a recoverable water/resource stream.

children.title: Wastewater characterization
children.description: Students learn the influent properties that control treatment design.

children.title: BOD, COD, TSS, nutrients, and pathogens
Preliminary and primary treatment
children.description: Students study the first solids and debris removal stages.

children.title: Biological treatment
children.description: Students learn how microbes remove organic matter and nutrients.

children.title: Residuals and reuse
children.description: Students examine what happens after the main liquid stream is treated.

topics.title: Air Pollution and Control
topics.description: Air pollution engineering links emissions, atmospheric behavior, human exposure, and control technology. Students learn how to quantify pollutants and select controls.

children.title: Pollutant types and effects
children.description: Students identify key air pollutants and why they matter.

children.title: Particulate matter, ozone, NOx, SOx, CO, VOCs, and toxics
Emission sources
children.description: Students connect pollution to combustion, industry, transport, and area sources.

children.title: Atmospheric fate
children.description: Students learn how pollutants move and transform.

children.title: Control technologies
children.description: Students select devices and strategies for pollutant reduction.

children.title: Cyclones, scrubbers, filters, and electrostatic precipitators

topics.title: Solid Waste Management
topics.description: This section treats waste as a material-flow and public-infrastructure problem. Students learn how collection, diversion, treatment, and disposal systems are planned.

children.title: Waste generation and characterization
children.description: Students learn what is in the waste stream.

children.title: Municipal, commercial, construction, and organics streams
Collection and transfer
children.description: Students examine logistics and cost drivers.

children.title: Routing, transfer stations, and fleet considerations
Recycling and organics recovery
children.description: Students evaluate diversion strategies.

children.title: Landfills and disposal
children.description: Students learn engineered containment and long-term management.

topics.title: Hazardous Waste
topics.description: Hazardous waste requires careful classification, containment, treatment, and documentation. Students learn how engineering controls reduce risk across storage, transport, treatment, and disposal.

children.title: Hazard identification
children.description: Students learn what makes a waste hazardous.

children.title: Fate and transport
children.description: Students understand how hazardous contaminants move through systems.

children.title: Treatment and remediation
children.description: Students compare approaches to risk reduction.

children.title: Pump-and-treat, in-situ treatment, and monitored natural attenuation
Management and documentation
children.description: Students connect technical handling to compliance.

topics.title: Environmental Regulations
topics.description: This section gives students the rules-of-the-road for professional environmental engineering. The goal is not legal memorization, but knowing how regulations structure design, permitting, monitoring, and accountability.

children.title: Regulatory frameworks
children.description: Students learn the major areas of environmental law and standards.

children.title: Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act context
Permitting and compliance
children.description: Students learn how design connects to permits.

children.title: Standards and guidance
children.description: Students distinguish enforceable limits from guidance and best practice.

children.title: Engineering ethics
children.description: Students learn professional responsibilities around public welfare.

children.title: Duty to protect health and safety

topics.title: Risk Assessment
topics.description: Risk assessment turns exposure, hazard, and uncertainty into a basis for decisions. Students learn to estimate risk while recognizing assumptions and limits.

children.title: Hazard and dose-response
children.description: Students learn how toxicity information is interpreted.

children.title: Reference doses and cancer slope factors
Exposure assessment
children.description: Students estimate who contacts what, how much, and for how long.

children.title: Risk characterization
children.description: Students combine exposure and toxicity into interpretable risk metrics.

children.title: Risk communication and management
children.description: Students learn how results inform action.

topics.title: Sustainable Engineering
topics.description: Sustainable engineering asks students to design systems that work technically while reducing resource use and long-term harm. It turns environmental engineering from end-of-pipe control toward systems improvement.

children.title: Sustainability metrics
children.description: Students learn how to measure environmental performance.

children.title: Energy, water, carbon, materials, and land indicators
Life-cycle thinking
children.description: Students assess impacts beyond the immediate project boundary.

children.title: Resource recovery
children.description: Students learn how treatment systems can recover value.

children.title: Design integration
children.description: Students translate sustainability goals into design choices.

topics.title: Climate Change Impact
topics.description: This section connects climate science to environmental infrastructure design. Students learn to evaluate changing hazards, uncertain futures, and adaptation needs.

children.title: Climate hazards
children.description: Students identify hazards relevant to environmental systems.

children.title: Heat, wildfire smoke, and sea-level rise
Infrastructure vulnerability
children.description: Students assess how systems fail or degrade under climate stress.

children.title: Adaptation and resilience
children.description: Students learn strategies for flexible and robust design.

children.title: Design storms and updated IDF curves
Climate mitigation links
children.description: Students connect environmental engineering to emissions reduction.

topics.title: Environmental Justice, Green Infrastructure, and Resilient Community Systems
topics.description: This final section brings technical design into community context. Students learn to design with equity, distributed natural systems, and resilience rather than treating communities as afterthoughts.

children.title: Environmental justice foundations
children.description: Students learn how environmental burdens and benefits are unevenly distributed.

children.title: Community-centered engineering
children.description: Students practice incorporating lived experience and local priorities.

children.title: Green infrastructure
children.description: Students evaluate nature-based and hybrid systems.

children.title: Bioretention, rain gardens, bioswales, and permeable pavements
Urban tree canopy and heat reduction
Resilient community systems
children.description: Students connect infrastructure reliability to social capacity.

children.title: Co-benefits for health, mobility, and public space
